audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and that is exactly right: Divine Judgment is named the matchup-defining cooldown in seven places across the two layers - 'bait it, then kill', 'Forward steps wait for its downtime', 'Commit on Divine Judgment's cooldown' - and its duration is never given once. Neither is anything else in her kit.
audit.why: The number is the whole point here. Divine Judgment is 160/120/80s. At rank 1 that is a hundred and sixty seconds - baiting it out does not buy you a trade window, it buys you nearly three minutes in which she has no answer to a Riftwalk. 'Bait it, then kill' is a slogan until you know that; with the number it becomes the entire game plan. The supporting numbers matter too: Starfire Spellblade is 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s and deals bonus damage proportionate to your MISSING health, so it hits hardest exactly when you are trying to leave. Celestial Blessing is a flat 15s. Radiant Blast is 12/11/10/9/8s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: Divine Judgment's 160s written into the cooldown block, the Lvl 6 spike and the all-in block; Starfire Spellblade's missing-health scaling and 8s reset, Celestial Blessing's 15s and Radiant Blast's 12s added.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json (R 160/120/80; E: 'bonus damage proportionate to their missing health', cooldown 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, autoReset; W cooldown 15; Q 12/11/10/9/8)

audit.whatIsWrong: The page credits Kayle's ranged form to the wrong ability, in four places: spikes[1] 'Kayle's E goes ranged so she finally pokes from afar', early 'her E (Starfire Spellblade) only adds on-hit magic damage at melee range until it goes ranged at 6', mid "Kayle's E finally goes ranged", whys[2] 'before her E goes fully online'. Her attack range comes from Divine Ascent, the passive. Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack reset that adds missing-health damage and has no range component. Also, breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.why: It changes what you watch. A reader tracking her E for the range transition is watching a spell icon; the transition is actually a passive level threshold, so it arrives whether or not she casts anything, and it cannot be baited or played around. Two interactions were also missing entirely: Radiant Blast REDUCES THE RESISTANCES of everything it hits, so her follow-up chip lands harder after a Q connects rather than being flat chip; and Divine Judgment makes an ALLY invulnerable, so she can spend her 160-second answer on someone else - which is the one thing that opens her up.
audit.corrected: Range reattributed to Divine Ascent, Starfire Spellblade described as the missing-health auto reset it is, Radiant Blast's resistance shred added, and Divine Judgment's ally-targeting noted. Silence removed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json (P Divine Ascent: 'progressively gains Attack Speed, Move Speed, Attack Range'; E: no range component; Q: 'reducing the resistances of all hit'; R: 'makes an ally invulnerable')

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts its own explanations at three consecutive stages. win[3] reads Kayle while whys[3] says 'Levels 4-5 are a wash... so it is even'. win[4] reads Skill while whys[2] says 'Level 6 is your flip'. win[5] reads Kayle while spikes[2] calls the first-item stage 'this is your cleanest all-in' and whys[4] says 'you out-tempo a low-AP Kayle'. As stored, no stage in the chart reads Kassadin at all.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 63.64%. The sample is thin at 11 games, but the shape the prose describes is the standard Kayle curve and it is coherent: she bullies a melee Kassadin through level 5, he owns the window from 6 until her second item, then she out-scales him permanently. A chart that awards her every stage cannot describe that, and it disagrees with three of its own whys.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 set to Skill, Level 6 and First item flipped to Kassadin, all in both layers. 2+ items left with Kayle, where every source already agrees.

audit.why: Celestial Blessing heals Kayle and the nearest ally on a flat 15-second cooldown, which is short enough to fire twice inside a single extended trade. That is what makes a slow Kassadin all-in fail against her even when the burst maths look fine.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named against Celestial Blessing in the all-in block.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kayle.json (W: 'heals and grants Move Speed to herself and the nearest ally', cooldown 15)

edits.before: "At levels 1-5 Kayle is a pure melee with no ranged attacks yet — her only reach is Radiant Blast (Q), a ground-targeted slow-and-mark, while her E (Starfire Spellblade) only adds on-hit magic damage at melee range until it goes ranged at 6. Do not throw Q to trade — you cannot afford the mana and her Q mark/slow lets her stick. Farm defensively, use Nether Blade on minions and on her when safe to keep your pool topped, and lean on Void Stone's 15 percent magic reduction to soak her on-hit chip. edits.after: At levels 1-5 Kayle is a pure melee - her only reach is Radiant Blast (Q), a 12-second ground-targeted slow that also strips resistances off everything it clips, so her follow-up chip lands harder than it looks. Starfire Spellblade is an 8-second auto reset that scales with your MISSING health, which is why she hurts most when you are already trying to leave. Even so she out-trades you here, because your Null Sphere is short-ranged, eats your mana, and you have no Riftwalk until 6. Do not throw Q to trade. Farm defensively, use Nether Blade on minions and on her when safe, and lean on Void Stone's 15 percent magic reduction to soak her on-hit chip. Concede these levels; just do not die.

edits.before: "Level 6 is the real turning point — and it cuts both ways. Kayle's E finally goes ranged so she can poke you from a distance for the first time, but you unlock Riftwalk: a short blink that closes the gap, dodges ganks, and answers her step-ups. Your Q shield plus Void Stone's magic reduction blank a meaningful share of her on-hit chip, so trades stop being free for her. Through levels 4-5 keep farming with Nether Blade refunds — that is weather-the-storm, not fight time. The moment your first stall item (Catalyst into Rod of Ages) lands, you climb past her: she is still a squishy, low-AP carry with no two-item spike, so this is your one clean all-in — Riftwalk in, Q-shield her counter, Force Pulse, and burst her down before her ranged scaling comes online."
edits.after: Level 6 is the real turning point and it cuts both ways. Divine Ascent gives Kayle ranged autos for the first time, but you unlock Riftwalk: a 5-second blink that closes the gap, dodges ganks, and answers her step-ups. Your Q shield plus Void Stone blank a meaningful share of her on-hit chip, so trades stop being free for her. Through levels 4-5 keep farming with Nether Blade refunds - weather-the-storm, not fight time. The moment your first stall item lands you climb past her, because she is still a squishy low-AP carry. This is your one clean all-in: bait Divine Judgment first, since at 160 seconds a spent R leaves her defenceless for the rest of the wave - then Riftwalk in, Q-shield her counter, Force Pulse, and burst her.

edits.before: "Be honest — Kayle out-scales even you. By level 11 she hits Exalted (longer-range autos), at 16 Transcendent (full flame-wave waveclear), and her R, Divine Judgment, gives her several seconds of complete invulnerability that eats your entire Riftwalk-plus-Force Pulse combo and lets her DPS you down afterward. Your two-item assassin window that deletes most champions does NOT out-tempo hers; she spikes just as hard and out-ranges you. The whole game plan is to make her early irrelevant: snowball your level-6-to-first-item window into plates and a kill, force her off the wave, and end the game before she reaches two items and her R-protected ranged DPS takes over the map."
edits.after: Be honest - Kayle out-scales even you. By 11 she hits Exalted and at 16 Transcendent, and Divine Judgment gives several seconds of complete invulnerability that eats your entire Riftwalk-plus-Force Pulse combo and lets her DPS you down afterward. She can also spend it on an ALLY, so a Kayle protecting someone else is a Kayle with nothing left for you - watch where the beam lands. Buy Grievous Wounds too; Celestial Blessing heals her every 15 seconds. The plan is to make her early irrelevant: snowball level 6 to first item into plates and a kill, and end the game before her R-protected ranged DPS takes over.

notes: THE PACKET'S DEFECT WAS REAL: no cooldown appeared anywhere in either layer despite Divine Judgment being named the matchup-defining cooldown seven times. The number transforms the advice - Divine Judgment is 160/120/80s, so baiting it at rank 1 buys nearly three minutes, not a trade window. WRONG SLOT, four places: the page credits Kayle's ranged form to her E ('Kayle's E goes ranged so she finally pokes from afar'). Attack range comes from Divine Ascent, her PASSIVE, as she levels; Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack reset with no range component, and its bonus damage scales with the target's MISSING health, which is why she is most dangerous when you are already leaving. Two interactions were absent from both layers: Radiant Blast REDUCES THE RESISTANCES of everything it hits, and Divine Judgment can be cast on an ALLY - a Kayle who spends it protecting someone else has nothing left for you, which is the one crack in a 160-second cooldown. Grievous Wounds added against Celestial Blessing's flat 15s heal. LEVEL CHART: it contradicted its own explanations at three consecutive stages - win[3] Kayle against whys[3] 'a wash... it is even', win[4] Skill against whys[2] 'Level 6 is your flip', win[5] Kayle against spikes[2] 'this is your cleanest all-in'.
